{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Paul Chester Kainen''' is an American mathematician, an adjunct associate professor of mathematics, and the director of the Lab for Visual Mathematics at [[Georgetown University]].<ref>[http://math.georgetown.edu/faculty/ Mathematics faculty listing], Georgetown U., retrieved 2012-07-05.</ref> Kainen is the coauthor of a popular book on the [[four color theorem]]{{sfnp|Saaty|Kainen|1977}} and is also known for his work on [[book embedding]]s of [[graph theory|graphs]].{{sfnp|Bernhart|Kainen|1979}}

==Biography==
Kainen received his Bachelor of Arts degree from George Washington University in 1966 and was awarded the [[Ruggles Prize]] for Excellence in Mathematics.  He went on to get his Ph.D. from Cornell University in 1970 with [[Peter Hilton]] as his thesis advisor.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=9092}}</ref> Kainen's father was the American artist [[Jacob Kainen]].
